prize_parts.citation: for developing empirical methods to estimate demand and competition in differentiated-product markets, and dynamic models of industries

statement.case_for: Random-coefficients demand estimation with endogenous prices (Berry 1994; Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes 1995), together with Pakes's dynamic-industry framework, turned structural estimation of demand, markups and merger effects from a specialist exercise into routine practice. The methods are used well beyond IO, in trade, health, environmental and public economics, and in antitrust and merger review. The contribution is therefore both a methodological advance and one that changed what economists and regulators can credibly measure. The work is about thirty years old, so its durability and its limits are well documented. It has not been recognised by the Academy. The BLP core gives a defensible three-person attribution.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that this is primarily a methodological contribution, and the Committee may weight discoveries about economic phenomena more heavily. The three-person cap also excludes Bresnahan and Reiss, whose claim to the empirical-IO revolution is substantial, as well as Benkard and Levin. The candidate also drew support from only six of ten members who ranked it, with a lower count of top-three placements than B037, B001 or B013. That breadth gap deserves to be weighed against my own first-place ranking. I am an IO researcher, so I may be too generous toward this field.

responses.point: Ranks B022 first because the Berry inversion, BLP and Pakes's dynamic-games work changed how demand, market power and welfare are measured. He notes that Bresnahan and Reiss are excluded by the three-person limit.
responses.response: I agree on the core attribution. I also think the exclusion of Bresnahan and Reiss is a real cost, not just a technicality. I still prefer the BLP trio. Their contribution is the identifiable, jointly credited solution to endogenous prices in differentiated-product demand, whereas Bresnahan's and Reiss's contributions concern a somewhat different strand (market-structure inference and earlier demand-system and market-power work). I would not claim the credit split between BLP and Pakes's dynamic-games strand is settled.

responses.point: Ranks B022 sixth and notes that methodological prizes are less certain to rank above substantive discoveries. She also points out that credit extends to Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin.
responses.response: The distinction between method and discovery is the central objection to my preferred candidate. My answer is that BLP is not a purely technical refinement. It changed which quantities (own- and cross-price elasticities, markups, welfare effects of mergers) can be measured credibly from market data. It is used in regulatory and antitrust decisions, not only in academic papers. I accept that this argument weakens if the Committee wants a prize tied to a specific empirical finding. I would not argue that it should outrank a candidate with a clear substantive result on the same criteria.

responses.point: Ranks B004 first, arguing that Grossman and Helpman's protection-for-sale framework is foundational and general, while acknowledging that the empirical support is mixed.
responses.response: I agree that the Grossman-Helpman pairing has a very clean two-person attribution, which B022 lacks. I put more weight on a contribution that has been used constructively in the field for decades, and the mixed empirical record for protection-for-sale makes that harder to claim for B004. I do not think the gap is large, though, and I would not object strongly if the Committee preferred a trade-theory prize on attribution grounds.

responses.point: Ranks B037 first. He values the combination of task and skill-biased technology with credible trade-shock evidence, and notes that the cap forces out Dorn.
responses.response: B037 has the broadest support at this stage, and its policy relevance is clear. My own opening list named Autor, Hanson and Dorn instead of Katz, because the China-shock strand is the most cleanly attributable part and Dorn is a co-author of those papers. My reservation is that the technology and trade-shock strands may be two contributions that are being bundled. The persistence and size of the China-shock effects are also still debated. I would therefore keep it as an alternative, not as my preferred choice, and I am not asking others to adopt my ordering.

uncertainties: Whether Bresnahan should displace Levinsohn, or whether the cap should be read as pointing toward a narrower award around BLP and Pakes.
Whether the Committee treats this as a method that changed practice or as a discovery about economic phenomena, and how it weighs the structural-versus-reduced-form debate.
How the narrower support for B022 should weigh against the broader, cleaner two-person case for B001 and the broader support for B037.
I did not verify any sources independently and rely on the supplied profile and colleagues' opening statements.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to the credited names of B022 is apparent from my supplied profile. Disclosed for transparency only: I work in industrial organisation, which is adjacent to this candidate; I co-authored with Committee chair John Hassler and former chair Tore Ellingsen (IJIO 2026); and my spouse is a former Swedish prime minister, which is a public fact with no apparent bearing on any shortlisted candidate. None of these is adjudicated here.
